\paragraph{Compounding (lineage vs.\ matched reset): a bounded null at the trajectory level.}
\textbf{Estimand and unit of replication.} The independent replicate is a \emph{trajectory} (one seed, one base checkpoint, one held split, one accumulated adapter), \emph{not} a round: rounds inside a run share all of those and are serially dependent. We therefore report the trajectory-level mean as the primary estimand, a cluster-robust (CRVE) estimate on the round-level data clustered on trajectory as a secondary check, and the naive round-level pooling only so the correction is auditable. Measured intra-trajectory correlation is ICC${=}$0.093 (design effect 1.28, so the naive $n{=}228$ rounds carry the evidence of roughly 178 independent observations).
\textbf{Result.} Pooled over 57 trajectories (228 round-comparisons), lineage$-$reset ${=}$ $-0.010\,[-0.035,+0.016]$, TOST-equivalent at $\delta{=}0.05$ with $\mathrm{BF}_{01}{=}5.6$ --- \emph{moderate} evidence for the null. The cluster-robust estimate agrees ($-0.002\,[-0.024,+0.020]$, $\mathrm{BF}_{01}{=}7.4$). For contrast, the naive round-level pooling would report $-0.002\,[-0.020,+0.016]$ with $\mathrm{BF}_{01}{=}14.7$; that number is an artifact of treating correlated rounds as independent and we do not claim it. The conclusion is unchanged in sign and verdict, but the strength of evidence is \emph{moderate}, not strong.
\textbf{Robustness.} Restricting to trajectories with $\geq3$ rounds (36 runs) and to full-length $\geq6$-round trajectories (29 runs) leaves the pooled verdict EQUIV with $\mathrm{BF}_{01}\!\approx\!5.9$ and $4.9$ respectively, so the null is not an artifact of short or interrupted runs.
\textbf{Per round}, lineage$-$reset shows a \emph{transient} early advantage (rounds 1--2) that decays to $\approx0$ by round 3 --- consistent with a one-step data-channel gain rather than recursive compounding.
\emph{Scope:} rejection-sampling SFT (not full RL/GRPO); Qwen2.5-Coder family; the bank and budgets described above. A denser-reward variant (speedup-weighted rejection sampling, top-quartile-by-roofline kernels only) shows the same null on 2 seeds, so the result is not an artifact of the weakest selection rule --- but at that $n$ it is an indication, not a test.
\textbf{What this null does and does not license.} It is a \emph{bounded} null: the compounding advantage is contained within $\pm 0.05$ at the tested scales. It is \textbf{not} yet evidence that the harness \emph{could} have registered compounding. The randomized coverage-transplant $2\times2$ we originally designed proved computationally infeasible on the crash-isolated grader (${\sim}12$\,s per kernel-grade put round~0 alone beyond 2.5\,h), so the coverage \emph{mechanism} is established indirectly from the $p$-maps, the sharpening geometry and the 0-score forensics. A tractable coverage-injection positive control has since been run on H100 and returned flat in \emph{both} arms --- but on that hardware the primary metric is saturated (75\% of non-zero frozen-base calibration scores within $\pm0.01$ of parity; see the instrument-validity section), so it licenses no conclusion in either direction. \textbf{A control that is flat because the instrument cannot move is not a control.} Re-running it under a metric with demonstrated range on that hardware remains the decisive outstanding experiment.

\paragraph{(methods) Pre-fix runs are excluded as uninterpretable, not counted as nulls.}
An early diagnostic isolated a generation-after-SFT failure: on the same model, the frozen base (adapter off) scored held-out $C{=}0.319$ and a freshly-attached \textbf{zero-update} LoRA generated normally ($C_{\text{train}}{=}0.259$, $C_{\text{held}}{=}0.388$), but after a single SFT step \emph{both} train and held-out $C$ fell to exactly $0.000$. A zero-step adapter evaluating correctly, plus the collapse hitting the \emph{training} tasks too, identifies this as a harness fault (SFT NaN-gradient path) rather than catastrophic forgetting. Runs predating the fix (grad-finiteness guard $+$ lr $10^{-5}$, plus a process-group kill on per-kernel timeout) are therefore excluded by a canonical-seed allowlist and contribute to no statistic in this paper; they are uninterpretable, not nulls.


\subsection{Search vs.\ training (the headline positive)}
\paragraph{Finding (i): at matched compute, best-of-$N$ search beats lineage self-training.} lab\_compounding compares, each round, the lineage model against frozen-base best-of-$N$ at the \emph{matched cumulative} generation budget $k(r{+}1)$, so the contrast is compute-matched by construction. Analysed at the \textbf{trajectory} level (the independent replicate; see the compounding estimand above), pooled over 57 trajectories comprising 228 round-comparisons, lineage$-$bestof$N = -0.111\,[-0.138,-0.083]$ --- the 95\% CI \emph{excludes zero} --- and verified search beats lineage in 84\% of \emph{runs} (76\% of rounds). The cluster-robust estimator (which weights rounds rather than runs) gives $-0.142$\\,[-0.163,-0.120] --- a larger effect of the same sign, its interval also excluding zero. Per scale: 0.5B $-0.123\,[-0.191,-0.056]$, 1.5B $-0.114\,[-0.157,-0.071]$, 3B $-0.123\,[-0.179,-0.067]$, 7B $-0.018\,[-0.122,+0.085]$. Scales with $<5$ trajectories (14B) are reported but not interpreted individually. Unlike the compounding result (a bounded null), this is a \emph{significant positive}: verified search converts a fixed generation budget into capability more efficiently than distilling that same budget into weights. The practical corollary (with the coverage gap) is that in domains with cheap dense verification and low cross-task transfer, compute is better spent on search than on self-training.


\subsection{Mechanism and self-play}
\paragraph{Mechanism (133 WHY-RSI probes, 0.5--15B).} Two internal gates, reported as \emph{associations}
(not yet causal). (1) \textbf{Correctness wall:} small ($<$2B) models cross \emph{less frequently} than $\geq$2B models
--- overall 97/133 runs (73\%) emit at least one correct kernel; below the wall the SFT set is empty so weight drift
$\to 0$. (2) Among wall-crossers, compounders (28/133) are associated with higher sustained LoRA drift and retention;
apparent compounding peaks at mid-scale 2--8B, while the largest models drift most yet saturate against the task
roofline (no-headroom). See the internal-failure causality DAG (Fig.~\ref{fig:cz_internal_dag}).

\paragraph{T5 self-play (3-arm S/F/L): an author-yield failure, not a measured null.} The primary metric is $L-F$ (author co-evolution). Open-weight arm: 24 runs; closed/API arm: 11 runs. \textbf{The binding problem is author yield, not solver capacity.} Interpreting $L-F$ requires the live author to have actually produced accepted, novel, valid tasks; we set a floor of 5 accepted model-authored tasks. Only 6/24 open runs and 5/11 closed runs clear it. Every closed run reports exactly $L-F=0.0$ (10/11 rows), including runs whose author proposed 36--37 tasks across 24 rounds --- a pattern that indicates the co-evolution channel never engaged rather than that it engaged and returned zero. The dedicated self-play \emph{diagnosis} run (Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, 8 rounds) authored \textbf{zero} valid tasks in every round, so all of its per-round diagnostics (authored solve-rate, trivial/unsolvable fractions, headroom) are undefined (8/8 rounds null) and all three arms scored $C{=}0$. We therefore report it as an \emph{author-yield failure}, and explicitly do \emph{not} draw the ``authored tasks are either trivial or unsolvable'' conclusion from it --- that bimodality is a hypothesis the run was unable to test. \textbf{Previously quoted positives do not survive this floor:} starcoder2-15b $L{-}F{=}+0.232$ on \textbf{1} accepted authored task over 6 rounds; deepseek-coder-6.7b-base $L{-}F{=}+0.154$ on \textbf{3} accepted authored tasks over 3 rounds. We therefore report T5 as \emph{undefined at the current author yield} and place no $L-F$ value in the headline claims. The honest finding this section supports is narrower and still useful: \emph{free-form task proposal collapses}; without constrained, executable task mutation an author does not manufacture a frontier, so self-play cannot be tested at all. Structured mutation with validity and learnability gates is the prerequisite experiment, not an extension.

\paragraph{Coverage-vs-scale $p$-maps (the wall is a sampling artifact).} For each model we sample
$K$ kernels per task and estimate per-task $p_K(t)$, coverage set $\{t:p_K(t){>}0\}$, and unbiased pass@1/pass@$K$
(Chen et al.). Coverage jumps sharply across the sub-2B ``wall'' (0.5B$\to$3B: 14\%$\to$83\%), and \emph{below}
the wall pass@$K\gg$pass@1 (12--17$\times$) --- the wall is a low-per-sample-probability \emph{sampling}
artifact, not absent capability. At 14B the ratio collapses to $\sim$1$\times$ (pass@1${=}0.66$): the teacher is
reliably-per-sample, not sampling-limited. Rejection-sampling self-training can only \emph{sharpen} the thin
low-$p$ frontier a small model already covers; it cannot manufacture the coverage a larger model has --- the
mechanism behind the compounding null.

\paragraph{Sharpening geometry (why compounding is coverage-limited).} Partitioning tasks by per-sample success $p_K(t)$ into \emph{unreachable} ($p{=}0$), \emph{sharpenable} ($0{<}p{<}0.2$, where rejection-sampling self-training can add signal), and \emph{reliable} ($p{\geq}0.2$) reveals the mechanism directly: at small scale the unreachable mass dominates (0.5B: 86\%) and the sharpenable band is thin; it \emph{peaks at mid-scale} (3B/7B: 59--79\% sharpenable --- the only regime with substantial material for self-training, consistent with where transient compounding appears); and at 14B it collapses as mass moves to \emph{reliable} (86\%), leaving nothing to sharpen. Self-training can only move the sharpenable band --- thin below the wall, absent above it --- so it cannot manufacture coverage.

\paragraph{Weight-level mechanism (WHY-RSI probes, open models).} LoRA drift, retention and generation diversity across scale localise where self-improvement is gated internally, reported as \emph{associations} rather than established causal gates. Below 2B, weights barely move (drift $+0.019$, retention $0.013$): the correctness wall is crossed only 54\% of the time, and below the wall an empty SFT set means \emph{no gradient to drift on}. The 2--8B band crosses almost always (100\%) and shows the highest rate of apparent compounding (50\% of runs) --- the only regime with both coverage and headroom. At $\geq$8B drift is \emph{largest} ($+0.596$) yet the compounding rate falls to 23\% and diversity collapse reaches 62\%: motion without progress near the task roofline. When drift occurs it localises to \emph{late} layers (task adaptation) and the held-family transfer gap is $\approx0$ (no transferable meta-skill). \textbf{Note on diversity:} among wall-crossers, compounders have \emph{lower} mean generation diversity than flat runs (0.41 vs.\ 0.52), so on this bank ``diversity collapse causes the null'' is \emph{not} supported --- compounding here looks like productive convergence onto a good basin. Diversity contraction remains a plausible cross-round option-value lock (Discussion), but it is an association whose clean test is a diversity-preserving intervention we have not run.

\paragraph{Task-3 procedure self-modify: closed-source failure analysis (behavioural mechanism).} Frontier models each rewrite their own optimisation strategy library $+$ verified kernel archive over rounds. Restricting to the 5 runs with $\geq$3 completed rounds, the gain is overwhelmingly \emph{one-shot}: mean round-0 jump +0.218 vs.\ mean subsequent $\sum(F_g{>}0)$ +0.068 (76\% of total gain arrives at round 0), and 60\% of those runs are non-recursive (ceiling / one-shot-plateau / stall). The archive saturates by round 1--2 (strategy-space exhaustion); the only sustained-improvement cases start from low $Q_0$, i.e.\ they consume headroom rather than demonstrate recursive self-insight. Strategy convergence (Jaccard over self-written strategies) is only 0.12 --- models write \emph{diverse} strategies yet still plateau, so the bottleneck is not strategy homogeneity but the inability to convert strategies into compounding capability. \textbf{Not interpreted:} DeepSeek-V3.2 (1 round), Kimi (2 rounds), Opus-5 (1 round) did not complete enough rounds to distinguish a genuine ceiling or self-degradation from an interrupted run; in particular the apparent DeepSeek-V3.2 ``self-degrade'' is a single-round artifact and is not a finding. This mirrors the weight-RSI compounding null on the API track.

\paragraph{0-score failure forensics (where the wall actually is).} Sampling $K$ candidates per task and classifying \emph{why} each scores zero shows the sub-3B ``correctness wall'' is really a kernel-\emph{formation} wall: the dominant failure is \texttt{no\_extract} (no parseable \texttt{ModelNew} ever emitted; 57--96\% of candidates) followed by \texttt{syntax\_error} (truncated mid-kernel), \emph{not} runnable-but-wrong kernels. Reading the chains: 0.5B mode-collapses into off-task repetition, 1.5--3B truncate or \emph{hallucinate APIs} (e.g.\ \texttt{torch.gelu}), and only at $\geq$3B do \texttt{wrong\_output} (silently incorrect) and \texttt{correct} appear. The failure locus moves \emph{downstream} with scale (incoherence $\to$ truncation $\to$ API-hallucination $\to$ wrong-output $\to$ correct): each scale step advances the model one pipeline stage, which is \emph{why} coverage is formation-gated below the wall (cf.\ the $p$-map coverage curve).

\subsection{Thesis and framing (frontier-panel guidance)}
\textbf{Primary question (reframed):} \emph{Does verified self-improvement compound?} KernelAscent is a
\textbf{roofline-grounded, compute-matched testbed} for RSI dynamics: GPU kernels are the rare domain where
reward is objectively verifiable and the performance ceiling is \emph{physically known} (the roofline), so
headroom is an absolute number. The central artifact is a \textbf{lineage-vs-reset $\times$ scale phase
diagram} with matched total compute and a \emph{positive control} (oracle-injected correct kernels, so a null
is provably distinguishable from a broken harness). \textbf{We must report that this control has not yet fired} on the hardware and metric of the headline: on H100 it exhausted its task set by round~2 and returned a delta of exactly zero, so the null is reported as not admissible under our own gate rather than as a validated null. The benchmark's contribution is that it \emph{separates}
the bottlenecks of kernel-code self-improvement --- generation, selection, weight-update, and curriculum ---
and makes purported self-improvement hard to fake. Secondary results: an internal correctness probe beats
uniform-random selection at matched \emph{generation} budget ($+0.124\,[+0.029,+0.218]$ clustered on base
checkpoint) but against no stronger comparator, and its within-task ranking estimand is \emph{unmeasured}
because per-candidate scores were not retained; the correctness wall below $\sim$2B is a sampling/formation
artifact rather than absent capability; and the self-play author collapses without structured task mutation,
leaving $L-F$ undefined rather than measured. We distinguish \emph{persistent} self-improvement (inherited
updates help) from \emph{recursive} improvement (updates improve future training), and claim only what the
controls support.
Prioritized next runs: (1) a leakage-resistant probe replication on a larger, family-split task bank with a
\emph{within-task} ranking metric and matched-candidate comparators (random / length-normalized likelihood /
compile-filter); (2) a staged lineage-vs-reset debug to recover or drop the compounding claim; (3) T5
self-play with author validity + learnability gates before extending trajectories.
